# HISTORICAL (superseded by the capacity correction f01e64e79) — D3 Task49: sector-height public-baseline observer: residual JOIN finding CORRECTED, UNREVIEWED and UNRUN (7 November 2026)

The SAME reviewer closed `ENV-SECTOR-HEIGHT-OBSERVER-COMPLETE-1` and `ENV-SECTOR-HEIGHT-BASELINE-RUN-1` and kept `ENV-SECTOR-HEIGHT-OBSERVER-JOIN-1` open: the first correction assumed a callback order the real funnel does not have. Source `eff3b4b332ec3592ae57c89f0a3d9bf426087e0b` over `4901b6880` corrects it; packet [reference/d3-entity-collision/sector-height-public-baseline-join-fix](eech-campaign/reference/d3-entity-collision/sector-height-public-baseline-join-fix/README.md). Earlier packets stay literal. **The finding and `sector-height-host-move-open-facts` stay OPEN**: the same reviewer must assess the delta and a baseline must actually run. No physical move, no native acceptance, no Windows, native or campaign launch.

What was wrong, observed on the real funnel order: `campaign_place_insert (en)` nests the host's INSERT and the entity's first fixed or city state statement before it returns, so the observer record, opened after the call, met that statement with no record and a baseline could never be whole; and a city building, placed twice (its city's list, then its sector, the placement map preferring the sector key once it exists), was classified child-only by family. Now the insert hook stands before the call (it only records; no production call, getter or order moves), and a statement's stage comes from the key the placement map itself chose: a sector-stage statement joins its sector record, a city-list-stage statement is counted apart, any other family under a child key is a failure, and a statement with no record is still refused.

Evidence: a new control runs the REAL staged placement map over scripted entities and a scripted host with the real recorder core, C report and Rust converters, reading the hook order from the ACTUAL staged patch text so the control and the code cannot disagree; it covers fixed, city, a building in both stages, two same-family records of one sector with interleaved statements, relink, a slot freed while listed and genuinely unjoined placements. It was RED against the d74 placement of the insert hook and against the d74 family-only rule, then GREEN. Final Linux checks (fmt, strict clippy for the default, funnel and observer sets, the funnel, chain, cap and real-C controls, the driver guards) ran between actual PRE and POST input maps of 3967 files with every row equal; the earlier closed results are reused by an exact changed-input join (9 rows changed, 2 added, 3956 identical). Root's feedback (a CI readback of the preceding head, all nine jobs success) appeared after the PRE map and was read at the freeze: a timing miss, retained. The new code needs its own CI. One process-learning bullet was appended to `docs/governance/D3-FIVE-WHYS-20261102.md`: an observer must follow the actual nested callback order and every placement stage, and its test must bind that order from the staged source before the freeze.

Limits: the control runs the real placement map but not the real `en_list.c`, the entity heap, the roster provider, the host or the `eech-dc` binding; the observer DLL is not assumed result-neutral; no -O2, signalling-NaN or exhaustive-census claim. The campaign resolves the key to its entity (`mb_hostplace.c`, `mb_hostplacemap.h`) and its real sector list is only a conformance mirror: a disagreement, an unknown, ended or misplaced key, or a missing roster is a NAMED refusal (`entity_scan.roster_mirror`, `entity_scan.roster_key`, `entity_scan.key`, `roster.*`), never an end, a miss or a fallback. A hosted mobile's record is made current before the sector insertion of a relink (`campaign_movement_place` moved earlier in `vh_vec3d.c`/`ac_vec3d.c`, still exactly one placement). Heap release removes a still-placed entity; a boot resets the keys and the host's roster. The hook adds refusals only for states in which the host and the campaign disagree (a double insertion, the removal of an entity that was never placed, an entity with no position, a hosted mobile whose record stands in another sector than the one the campaign inserts it into, an ended or unknown key); none is meant to be raised by a supported creation, unpack, relink or release path, and only a native run can show that none is.

# D3 L2 handshake corrections after the 12a review (2 November 2026, source only)

Task50 / PR110. The review of `12a642d54e` cleared the carry-over correction and found three handshake groups; Root's strict lint on that source added a type-complexity refusal. This entry records the SOURCE corrections. NOTHING here is built or run; the static checks made (strict-count simulation of all 33 staged patches, bracket balance) are not compile or runtime evidence. The 12a default recordings Root collected (3025 scenes, literal against the retained original lists) stay at their own identity. Task50 and whole D3 stay open.

1. Bounded announcement. A provider's walk announcement is one transaction: at most 4096 files (the campaign's own limit), each (scene, directory) once, steps one after another from 0, every domain checked before any state changes, and a closed announcement is final (a late step, a second end or a new walk is refused; a new provider is a new transaction). Unit tests exercise the state machine with a small cap; real-VM witnesses exercise the lifecycle, the duplicate, the out-of-sequence step, the over-long name, the scene domain and the closed walk. The 4096 limit of the host and of the campaign are tied by a source test.

2. Traversal completion. The staged traversal now ends with a check that every announced position was opened, each either read by `read_scene` or explicitly SKIPPED, and none outstanding. The original's own skip is characterised in source: `read_custom_scene` reads a scene only for versions -1 to -3 and otherwise logs and returns (tests read the original and pin it); the skipped branch consumes its position as skipped, claims no row and asks the host nothing, and opening a file while another is neither read nor skipped stops by name.

3. Replay initialisation and the pinned installation. `host.model` no longer loads the sorted custom history first. The database's own questions (object count, database definitions) and the acceptance of the announcement come from an INVENTORY store that reads no custom scene file; the final store is built once, from the announced order, after the announcement closes; no final answer (scene, triangle, route, custom definition) is given before that, and a sorted store is built only when a tool asks with no announcement, after which an announcement is refused. A real-parser fixture of 1600 custom scenes shows a read order that fits the original's room of 2000 objects where the sorted order does not (the 1000-name history fills before a shared name), loading by inventory and by the announced order while the sorted load is refused by name. The installation is pinned as an absolute path when the provider is registered (or when first needed, if the argument was not there yet) and replay uses that path: a relative root, a changed working directory or a changed host argument selects nothing else; a witness runs with a relative root from another directory and a mutated argument.

4. The six-value callback tuple has a named type for the strict lint. The nine-field metadata counters, the exact carry-over, T2 through the original add_new_animation, the truthful names, the true-backing hooks and the reached controls are unchanged. Root owns every build, native run and review.

# D3 L2 phase corrections after the 32b review (2 November 2026, source only)

Task50 / PR110. The same review of `32b39b99c4` left two residual phase findings, and Root's live gates added a build warning and a strict-lint refusal. This entry records the SOURCE corrections. NOTHING here is built or run; the static checks made (strict-count simulation of all 31 staged patches, bracket balance) are not compile or runtime evidence. The literal comparison Root made of source 32's default recordings with the retained original lists (3025 scenes, 95 listed, 2742 empty, 188 absent, 510 ordered ids, literal) stands at its own identity and says nothing about these changes. Task50 and whole D3 stay open.

1. Definition identity and the real walk order. The original walks `OBJECTS` with `_findfirst` / `_findnext`, which here is the file system's own, unsorted, order (`eech_win32.c`), and what a custom definition sees depends on it: the number the first named object takes and the table object it replaces, the per-directory history of named objects, which definition of a scene is read last. Core keeps that walk unchanged and now ANNOUNCES it to the host before reading any file (a pre-walk of the same enumeration, one step per file: scene, position, directory name; `CUSTOM_ORDER`), verifies at each file it opens that it is the one announced at that position, and names a custom definition by that position. The host replays its definitions in the announced order (`load_in_order`, history reset per directory as the original does) and refuses a file the walk names that it lacks, names twice, or never reaches; a position of another scene is refused. A sorted walk is only the order when none is announced (tools). The distinguishing fixture is a scene whose object is named by hex number: the table's object 4 or the named object that replaced it, according to which file was walked first, shown by independent public views (scene bounds computed at read time) as well as by the headers. This is NOT a proof that the host's sorted order equals the campaign's; the host does not claim it.

2. Header carry-over. `read_object` assigns counts, bounds, radius and buffers and never `culling_normals_offset`. The host store keeps the row's value when an object is read into an existing row (binary-hex override; the first named object), and Core clears only what `read_object` assigns and remembers a described row it replaced; when the new object is described, the offset the row kept must equal the host's, or the engine stops (`[model-provider:object.carry]`). A real-parser fixture gives table objects non-zero offsets and checks the override, the first named object (carried) and the second (fresh, zero).

3. Counters. The metadata row has a ninth field, `rows_replaced` (a described row taken over by a new number): rows holding a description are `rows_filled - rows_replaced`; the horizon driver and its tests validate it. 4. Dead state removed: the scene's own approximation and shadow lists (the facts of each definition replaced them); no allow, no dummy read. The repeated override-name type is a named alias for the strict lint.

The 32b-built T2 comparison, the truthful names, the fifth-argument transport and the changed-control checks are unchanged. The unknown-name control can already resolve to 0 in the reference; it is no causal change until compared with a healthy run. Root owns every build, native run and review; fresh roots are Root's.

# D3 original animation-list driver: coherence correction (1 November 2026): UNBUILT, UNRUN

The independent review cleared the observer's C and hooks and found one driver and test coherence group, corrected in `lua/model-animation-characterization.lua` and its tests only; the C fixture, hooks,
production, model, route, kernel and public feature plumbing are exactly as at `4485`. The Root's 4485 builds are on their OWN source (Windows 0, Linux still running) and there is no native run of the
observer yet; the buffer cut at `abfda86326` stays finite-closed on its own actuals and is not whole Task50 or D3.

* **Headers joined to rows.** `scenes_read` must equal the scenes whose rows are not `absent` or `unobserved` (the scenes the loader finished reading), checked after the last page and before the first page is
  read again; `unknown_scene` must be 0 and unchanged on every page (a nonzero count is malformed, not a note); generation, digest and `scenes_read` must be the same on every page.
* **Row domains from the emitter's own states.** `listed`: 1..4096 ids, `filled` = `count`, allocation at least `count` (exactly `count` for a declared `file` list); `empty`: no count, allocation or filled entry;
  `absent` and `unobserved`: no source and no content; every other outcome has a source. Nothing a valid retail list could not meet is required; an unsupported outcome is still written and NOT MEASURED.
* **Clock.** Read before anything is asked and after the last answer: a table with finite single-precision `elapsed_seconds` and `time_of_day_seconds` and a whole 32-bit `day`; a missing, text, NaN,
  infinite, fractional or out-of-range value is malformed before the next engine call, and both readings must be equal. The checked values are written. No wall clock or temporal oracle is added.
* **Tests.** A coherent 99-scene multi-page capture (96 + 3 scenes) passes; damaged later pages (unknown scene, scenes read, digest, generation, echo, order, missing row, incoherent row), headers whose total
  the rows do not show, a first page that saw an unknown scene, the row-domain forms and the bad or moved clocks are malformed or not a success and stop at the first bad evidence.
* **Digest scope, stated honestly.** The page digest covers the recorded state and the verified list projection (status, count, filled entries, ids), not every emitted field (source, allocation and success flag
  are not in it); "nothing moved" rests on that digest, the byte-for-byte re-read of the first page and the clock, not on a full-row or table invariance claim. This also qualifies the entry below.
* **Why this characterisation matters (Root's source proof, `model-animation-required-consumer-source-abfda86326-20261101.json`):** `en_anim.c` `set_local_entity_id_number` derives the digit count and
  modulo from the animation membership, seeding the entity id number and campaign significant digits. No metadata ownership has moved; raw legacy ids stay private to this fixture, and the shipping protocol
  is unchanged.

findings, all closed in SOURCE here and not yet built or run; no claim that every legacy reader is safe until the review of this delta.

* **P1, compiled aliased readers.** `3dtrans.c` (`transform_3d_object`, `transform_flat_3d_object`, `transform_unclipped_3d_object`, `transform_unclipped_flat_3d_object` read `object->points`;
  `transform_3d_object_surface` and `transform_unclipped_3d_object_surface` also read `current_object_3d_surface_point_list`) are called by `draw_wbuffered_3d_object` and its siblings BEFORE the
  guarded face heads, and by terrain and explosion drawing. Added named heads (`LR-reader-*`, 26 new, 66 in all): the scene funnel (`draw_3d_scene`, `draw_normal_scene_objects`,
  `draw_transparent_scene_objects`), the four object draws and three sub-object draws (`3dobjdrw.c`, `3dobjdrz.c`, `3dobjdrh.c`), the six translucent entries, the six transforms and
  `illuminate_3d_object_surface` (its alias is the retained NORMAL list, not a detached buffer; it is stopped as part of the visual family, not as a detached reader), and a leaf with no caller.
  Coverage is a one-off dominance scan over the compiled `modules/3d` callers, function-pointer tables included: of 41 unguarded functions that mention a buffer or an alias, 35 are dominated by a
  head and 6 are not and are explained (the horizon decode after the `LU1` stop, the loader's own NULL assignments and frees, the host-patched collision accessor, and a shadow-visibility local box).
  `3dline.c`, `3dstrail.c` and the terrain files use other structs' `points`. Not a claim about reachability.
* **P2, loader I/O.** The new skips no longer `fseek`: `campaign_model_loader_skip` reads past each region through a 4096-byte buffer with checked counts (64-bit byte count, no narrowing, no Windows
  32-bit `long`), and a short read stops by name (`[model-provider:object.loader]`); the custom polygon-face chunks must be read in full or stop by name (`campaign_model_loader_short`). Valid files
  read the same bytes in the same order (the original read them too), so counts, offsets, texture overrides, the validation phase, FP and RNG are unchanged. The legacy header reads stay unchecked.
* **P2, witness.** `lua/model-horizon-control.lua` now parses the exact C grammar of all three counters rows (names, field order, decimal integers within 0..2147483647, a deliberate bound for
  the Windows 32-bit `long` and Lua doubles), checks coherence (`metadata_rows` and each buffer count not above `rows`, `presence_mismatches` not above `presence_checked`), does NOT launch the
  unsupported reader when the residency or cache evidence is invalid, and accepts the stop only as the whole first line of the Engine-owned fatal error (prefix, named marker, operation and
  reason, equal to the actual CCC primary line). Tests add damaged forms of the first row and of the cause, and tie the driver's grammar and text to the C and the staged guard. The comment that

# D3 host route boundary: popread consumers of the position table (1 November 2026): SOURCE ONLY; NOT BUILT, NOT RUN

The Root's source inspection found one more required consumer gap: `popread.c` `insert_airport_fixedwing_routes` (and the other airfield insertion functions) read `route_waypoint_positions[current_route_waypoint_offset]`
from the deepest depth (`number_of_route_waypoint_positions - 1`) and step the offset down by fixed amounts (decrements at 2920, 2950, 2964 and so on), so a route with too few depths reads index -1 and below.
Correction (staged patches H19/H20 and `campaign_model_route_position_index`, marker `[model-provider:route.position]`): all 205 occurrences of that indexed expression in `popread.c` (the `WAYPOINT_ALTITUDE` macro is one of them)
now index through a check that returns the same index, once per expression and before anything is read, and stops the engine when the index is outside `[0, number_of_route_waypoint_positions)` or the table does not exist. Nothing
is clamped, defaulted or invented and no minimum depth per route kind is introduced. The six `route_waypoint_positions[count]` troop-route copies are bounded by the table's own count and are not wrapped; routegen.c's own
table writes are untouched. Original-profile build unchanged. Static check only: all 23 named routegen.c/popread.c host patches apply with their counts against the real sources in sequence (H20: 205 expected, 205 found, 0
unwrapped, 6 `[count]` left), and a scan of the 12 offset loops found no read that uses a loop's exit index except the intended floor (offset 3 after the `> 3` taxi loop); no build, test or run.

Control correction for the Root: with the earlier `route.start` guard a connected pure-black TWO-node route no longer reaches `popread` (both nodes are starts, none on a green face, so the old code's uninitialised
`primary_start_index` is now refused as `route.start`). The smallest route that passes the parser is THREE nodes: black start-middle, green middle-leaf (depth count 3). Give landing AND take-off that same answer with
identical coordinates (the take-off's leaf is within 3.0 of the single slot, so no swap). `validate_airport_links` (landing parse, slots, take-off parse) completes; the insertion then reads offsets 2, 1, 0 and the decrement
at 2964 makes it -1, so the expected result is `route.position` for depth -1 of a 3-entry table, before any read at -1. Run on the corrected build only. Together with the 24-tree swap control already given (`route.swap`),
these are source-derived inputs, not executed anywhere. Task50 and D3 remain In Progress; no finite or whole closure. The Root's `50e7f9d85` actuals (704/528 and repeats, short campaign, four topology controls, def6 FP) keep their
own source identity and are not proof of this change.

# D3 host route boundary: one residual P1, the end-slot swap's resolved indices (1 November 2026): SOURCE ONLY; NOT BUILT, NOT RUN

Review `independent-model-host-route-guard-actual-50e7f9d85-20261101.json` (SHA256 `583c29a2d09b5406d9ba976de665a855b22daac98b91a2e05be33a5a7841c2c2`, source `50e7f9d8578c7d283b6a47f01a0e2d09e24cfd2f`) closed the
other new guards and left ENV-HOST-ROUTE-BOUNDARY-2 (P1): `swap_waypoint_nodes` (the end-slot matching's swap) resolves table indices by its own searches and writes through them. Its tree swap searches
the start table from entry 1, so a swap that selects the primary tree (entry 0, the `node_index` 0 leaf) resolves to the logical start count; with 24 starts that is `waypoint_starting_nodes[24]`, and
only the original `ASSERT` stood before the write (the 4096-pass limit comes too late). Its same-parent swap reads two indices that are assigned only if the search finds the child.

Correction (staged patches H16..H18 and `campaign_model_route_swap_index`, marker `[model-provider:route.swap]`): H18 checks both resolved start-table indices (valid: 1 .. logical start count - 1, and inside the
24 entries) immediately BEFORE the original `ASSERT` and before either write; H16 initialises the two child indices to -1 and H17 checks both against the parent's logical child count (and the 24-entry table)
before the first write. The swap is not skipped, redirected or repaired: index 0 is still not searched for, partners are not chosen differently, and every swap the original takes runs the same statements in
the same order. Original-profile parser, provider, store, kernel, ABI, FP and earlier guards are untouched. Static check only: all 18 `routegen.c` host patches find their expected counts against the real
source in sequence, and the candidate fixture's R1/R2/R6 afterwards; no staging build, compile, test, engine or native run. The Root's own actuals at `50e7f9d85` (healthy captures, repeats, four
malformed-topology controls, the short campaign) are those of that identity and do not prove this correction.

One source-derived input recipe for the Root's guarded run (read from `popread.c` 2296..2360 and `routegen.c`, NOT executed anywhere): the campaign parses the fixed-wing landing route with no slots, takes the
absolute positions of its deepest-level nodes in `node_index` order as `matching_slots`, then parses the take-off route of the same airfield with them. Give BOTH routes the same 24 independent trees (a black
edge start-middle and a green edge middle-leaf: 24 starts, 72 nodes, depth 2, one `node_index` k per tree), the landing leaves at distinct positions more than 3.0 apart (slot k), and the take-off leaves the same
except that tree 0's and tree 1's leaf positions are exchanged. Then `match_end_slots` meets slot 0 with the tree-0 leaf (`node_index` 0) out of range, finds tree 1's leaf in range, `swap_waypoint_nodes` climbs both
to their roots (common parent NULL), searches the start table from 1: tree 1's root resolves, tree 0's does not (24). The corrected parser must stop with `route.swap` before any write. Run it only on the corrected build.
Task50 and D3 remain In Progress; the loader detachment is the next real work after the finite boundary is closed.

# D3 host route boundary guards: source-only follow-up to `8d1c79c8d` (1 November 2026): NOT BUILT, NOT RUN

Root's source read found a regression in the new progress guard: `set_node_indices` runs once from the parse and again from every end-slot swap (`swap_waypoint_nodes`, after it has invalidated the
indices), but the guard's count was reset only per parse, so a later invocation could legitimately start with as many nodes unnumbered as the last one ended with and be refused. H11b now begins the

explicit work limit of the host boundary, not derived from the original and not proof that a matching reaching it would never settle: a host route beyond it is unsupported and unmeasured, and a
baseline route reaching it would be a regression. Static check only: all 15 `routegen.c` host patches find their expected counts against the real source in sequence, and the candidate fixture's R1/R2/R6
afterwards; no staging build, compile, test, engine or native run. The Root's finite actuals remain those of `def6a9bde`; nothing here is acceptance of the guards. Task50 and D3 remain In Progress.

# D3 route observer: two residual P2 findings corrected in source (1 November 2026): SOURCE ONLY, NOT RUN

Base `9c525b42a`. Independent review `independent-model-original-route-correction-source-9c525b42a-20261101.json` (SHA256 `469dc51993d50c47a8b684545d07f88777a59e7996953c48c9af5df21931a216`, re-hashed) left two P2

hash and width reading against the repository's `max_width = 160`). Not touched, as asked: the native C observer, hooks, patches, production validators and physics, accepted data. The observer's native C/patches/entries
compiled in the Root's clean Windows route-fixture build of `9c525b42a` (reported: tool session 26133, exit 0) but are NOT run and NOT measured; no original retail data exists; the source gate stays false for these two fixes.

* ENV-ROUTE-OUTPUT-2 (`src/exclusive_output.rs`): `close` no longer treats a successful `sync_all` as the close. The `File` is consumed once: the data sync runs, the raw descriptor / handle is then taken out of the `File` and
  released by the platform's own close (`close` / `CloseHandle`), that result is returned, the release is attempted even if the sync failed, and the `File`'s drop therefore never closes a second time. A sync failure, a close
  failure, or both are reported, each named as what it is; the Lua writer still closes the owned output on every exit and keeps the primary driver failure. Exclusive `create_new` is unchanged. No dependency or generic IO layer.
  New unit tests: the sync/close combination rule; the REAL platform close with a value that is not a descriptor / handle (the operating system refuses it); a real file closed once with complete content. The driver
  tests' "close failed" cases remain a Lua stand-in and are documented as only the driver's reaction.
* ENV-ROUTE-PROTOCOL-2 (`route-characterization.lua`): the identity state is the whole token and must equal the literal `unique`, `unknown` or `ambiguous` (`unique-INVALID` and near misses are malformed); a face-local
  reference must be below its surface's point count; the repeated faces of a surface must carry the same colour, flags, polygon bit and point count; and a face-local reference must resolve to the same node wherever it
  recurs within a surface. These are consistency relations among captured records, not a second route solver. Seven new damaged controls extend the coherent-positive-first set (now 37 call controls, with the 14 summary
  controls: 51) plus four near-miss identity states; every earlier row, capacity, join and no-query-after-malformed check, the verbatim text handling, and all earlier controls are unchanged.

result stands as 4 passed / 1 failed (the false acceptance), and the old red raw logs record `docker-exit=0` only, so no numeric cargo exit is claimed for them (noted in the retained evidence file). The old `69ef` red text is

(2) Everything that asks a native HANDLE to do something (get playing, destroy, user data, play, play sequence, pause, continue, next, volume, position, pitch) stops the engine with `[env-sound:unsupported_native_handle]`, and everything that asks the SAMPLE STORE, the listener or the handle table (allocate, deallocate, create, destroy and load a sample, destroy all, update, orient the listener) with `[env-sound:unsupported_native_backend]`, before any native query, load, playback, destruction or state change; a made-up status or success is never returned for a live request and nothing is dropped. (3) One more refusal at the semantic lifetime boundary: `campaign_sound_lifetime_update` (`ss_hostenv.c`) refuses, after validating the host's answer and BEFORE writing the lifetimes, the host's kill or unlink decision for an effect that holds a handle, with the same handle tag, so the invalid-effect unlink and the kill never commit an unlink before the destroy; the valid-expiry status request keeps its own closed refusal `[env-sound:unsupported_handle_status]`. Sample loading is audited and not hidden behind the false capability: `load_application_sound_samples` and `destroy_application_sound_samples` run only when `application_sound_system_enabled` is TRUE, the host's availability is always FALSE (`campaign_sound_backend` refuses an "available" answer by name), and if they were ever reached `allocate_source_sound_samples` and `create_source_sound_sample` would stop by name before the first `fread`. # D3 sound handle status at a server expiry: the ORIGINAL buffer-absent idle handle characterization prepared (1 November 2026 UTC; SOURCE ONLY, UNBUILT, UNRUN, UNREVIEWED; CHARACTERISATION ONLY; a focused ORIGINAL control under Task 51 / PR 111, not whole-D3 closure; after f4c661fc4)

WHAT THIS ADDS. The one next missing physical coupling of the sound lifetime route: `se_updt.c update_server` (hosted block) gives a held handle to `campaign_sound_lifetime_update`; for an expired effect the HOST asks whether the handle is playing and the campaign answers with `host_handle_playing`, which is the REAL compiled `modules/sound/soundman.c get_system_sound_effect_playing` (it clears `effect->playing` and returns FALSE when `effect->sound_buffer` is NULL, and only otherwise asks the DirectSound buffer); a kill then reaches `se_dstry.c` and the REAL `destroy_system_sound_effect` (ASSERT used; release the buffer if any; clear `used`). The closed no-handle controls (cases 4 to 14) never reach that branch and printed it as unsupported. New fixture cases in group 14 (`csrc/eech_env_fixture.c env_snd_handle_case`, observer build only, explicit, PROCESS-ISOLATED): `21 handle_idle_buffer_absent_server_expiry` (the handle's `playing` starts 0) and `22 handle_idle_buffer_absent_stale_playing_server_expiry` (it starts 1: a SENSITIVITY MARKER, because the real getter writes the flag). Each builds ONE sound effect with the real constructor and the closed case-4 controlled descriptor (rate 4, size 20, restored), gives it a handle, and runs the real server routine of the function table at delta 2.0 up to three times, so the real host, getter and (on a kill) destroy run. The new public driver `lua/env-sound-handle.lua` (args `root= out= case=21|22 [scenario=]`) creates its evidence exclusively BEFORE boot, keeps the fixture's report whole in `<out>.case.raw` BEFORE validating any of it, checks a closed grammar (rows and keys in order, every value of its kind and domain), the case identity, that the record is as declared, that the cleanup left it released and that the tracking probe's records can follow one another and agree with the handle and cleanup rows, and judges nothing physical: its derived row only joins what the rows say. The guards are in `tests/env_sound_handle.rs` (scripted engine, real exclusive output; four tests: coherent idle-killed and playing-kept shapes, refusal and engine stop, 23 damaged reports each after its positive, argument/module/foreign-output refusals). Nothing production, no host ABI or schema, no flag, fallback, guard, loader, device or network line, and no existing case, oracle or driver changed.

THE HANDLE IS CONTROLLED TEST STATE, NOT AN ORIGINAL PRODUCT. In this headless process `create_single_system_sound_effect` returns NULL (`sound_system_initialised` is FALSE) and, when a buffer duplication fails, it RELEASES the record, so the original never yields a used record whose buffer is absent. The control instead fills element 0 of the REAL static zero-initialised array `current_system_sound_effects` (owned by `soundman.c`, never freed, its address valid through every real call and through a fatal unwind) as a real record would be filled (one sequenced sample, `used` TRUE, `sound_buffer` NULL, `user_data` NULL) with no COM pointer, vtable, sentinel address, global status override or audio code. It exercises the status getter's and the destroy's bodies for a buffer-absent record, not a backend: a PLAYING buffer needs a device that does not exist here and is NOT manufactured (printed as `env-snd-unsupported`), and the original constructor's handle is not reproduced.

MEMORY OWNERSHIP AND SIDE EFFECTS (for Root to validate). The only memory the control touches beyond the entity it creates is element 0 of that static array: refused before any change if the sound system is initialised or the element is in use; filled after the entity exists; on every path after that, an entity that survived and still holds the record is DETACHED first, a record still in use is released by the real destroy (the row says whether the original or the fixture did), and the element is zeroed, all BEFORE any row is written. The entity itself cannot be put back (the process is the isolation boundary; the end row says `process_isolated=required`). The lightning descriptor numbers and the frame delta are restored and the tracking switch is turned off before the rows on the normal-return path (see the correction above: a fatal unwind does none of that). No pointer or address is printed, but the PRIVATE raw report carries the probe's entity slot, entity index and position words (see the correction above). If the engine stops in a control (an invalid host answer), the engine is poisoned and the process ends with the record still held by the static array and the entity, which is valid memory. The shared seed and floating point state are not touched beyond what the real update routines already do in the closed case 4.

FOR ROOT (nothing run by the author; no actual exit is claimed). Build with the env-observer and env-fixture features (the case needs both). Guards: `cargo test --locked -p eech-world --test env_sound_handle` (plus the existing `env_sound_lifetime`, `env_sound_characterization` and `env_play_resumed_parent` suites, unchanged). Cause (source-read by the author, not a second public boot): the engine's boot (`eech_engine.c`) runs `brief_initialise_game` and the init screen's `full_initialise_game`, whose `init.c` calls `initialise_entity_system` (`en_init.c`, which calls `initialise_entity_functions`, and so the sound defaults); the same boot then calls `reinitialise_entity_system` (`eech_engine.c` line 273, `en_init.c`), which calls `initialise_entity_functions` again. So several C initialisations inside ONE public boot are the original's behaviour and count 2 is the coherent single-boot shape; the old message that equated a count above 1 with a second initialisation was wrong. The C and the native 8e are unchanged and this is not an M6 reload or reinitialisation acceptance.

Correction (`lua/env-play-resumed-parent.lua`): the driver observes the count in the first report after the completed boot, requires it to be at least one (zero is still a probe armed after the defaults or no census) and requires it unchanged in every later report (after the natural frames and after the fixture); a later change is refused as a further initialisation after boot. 2 is not hard-coded as a rule, the raw is kept as written, and the dropped, bad-point, unarmed, defaults-nondefault, dimension, phase and counter checks are as strict as before. `tests/env_play_resumed_parent.rs`: new `the_defaults_census_count_is_observed_after_boot_anchored_and_required_unchanged_afterwards` accepts coherent counts 1, 2 and 3 in natural, fixture and overload (with arbitrary later non-default type numbers) and refuses a first count of 0, an increase (1 to 2, 2 to 3), a decrease and a vanished count in the next report, and an increase across the fixture and the overload; the existing "armed too late" negative (count 0) still holds. (1) Digest join. The driver recomputes the fixture's FNV-1a digest (`env_play_digest` and `env_play_mix`: basis 2166136261, bytes least significant first, multiplier 16777619 modulo 2^32; the words are the number of sound children, the number of matching children, the completeness flag 1 and, per matching child, validity, update-list membership, LIFETIME word then VALID-LIFETIME word, which is NOT the printed order) from the target's counts and the printed `before` and `resumed` words and requires equality with `digest_before` and `digest_resumed`; the restored digest still has to equal the before digest. The multiplication is exact in doubles by two 16-bit limbs (every intermediate below 2^42) and the xor is bitwise. The selection is a pure function (`select_driver`) and its guard never mutates the process environment, so the parallel tests are unaffected.

# D3 rotor numerical correction after the 38b200b6c controls: narrowing at the original's float assignments and a run-time APU offset, in env_ref.c only (1 November 2026 UTC; SOURCE ONLY, UNBUILT, UNRUN, UNREVIEWED; after 38b200b6c)

Actual 38b200b6c gates: the pinned Linux and the native Windows runs each passed the kernel / control tests (3) and the witness tests (12), with complete captures, 1152 variant runs and 0 restoration mismatches each; CI had 6 successful jobs (strict lint and the Wine witness 12 included) and exactly three numerical failures, all unchanged oracle rows: BOTH i686 jobs, flight-model row 1 looping amplification expected `3f2aaaab` got `3f2aaaaa` and row 12 right turbine pitch expected `3f8e147a` got `3f8e147b`; Windows x64 under Wine (compiler `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc (GCC) 13-posix`, `__GNUC__` 13.0.0; its package lineage is separate), row 7 APU pitch expected `400ccccc` got `400ccccd`. The retained diagnostics are `rotor-control-CI38-{i686,i686-stack,windows-wine}-…json`. MEASURED in the emitted assembly: on i686 (gcc-12 12.4, x87, `__FLT_EVAL_METHOD__` 2) the kernel computes the slap level as `fdivs` (magnitude / 15.0), `fmuls` (times the looping level) and the bound, subtracts it from the looping level in the x87 register and stores the slap float only after the subtraction, while the unmodified control (collaborator calls between the statements) spills it as a float earlier and matches the oracle; `rrpm / 100.0` flows through `bound` into the `+ 0.6` with no first-assignment float store (the staged control has no marker at that assignment either, so its mismatch there is not evidence against restoring the store). On Wine the saturated branch of `bound (apu_rpm * 0.02, 0.0, 2.0) + 0.2` is the load of the constant `.LC70` = `0x400ccccd` (folded, with its narrowing, under the compiler's round-to-nearest) instead of the guarded run-time `addsd` and `cvtsd2ss` that Linux x86_64 executes (`0x400ccccc`).

The correction, `csrc/env_ref.c` only: (1) `ROTOR_STORE_FLOAT (destination, expression)` stores the unchanged expression into an addressable volatile float and reads it back, used at exactly the assignments those reds depend on: `acc_force`, the first `slap_amp`, and the first assignment of `left_turbine_pitch` and `right_turbine_pitch` (the left one for symmetry with the right, the same source contract); on an SSE target the value is already a float there, so nothing changes. (2) The `0.2` of the APU pitch is read from a function-local volatile double of the same value and type, so the addition and the conversion are run-time operations under the guarded round-toward-zero. No global flag, tolerance, oracle, control, target, guard, parser, `build.rs` or Core change; no per-case value. The U surrogate and the changed S control are not oracles and no complete original-engine assembly is claimed. Known finite scope, UNMEASURED: the other float assignments (the looping level and pitch, the turbine and APU levels, the left level times 1.2) and the saturated `bound (…, 0.0, 1.6) + 0.6` additions are unchanged because no measured red depends on them; the exact-target reds decide. Not run here: every build, test and CI. The changed source makes the earlier dd84 default and authority evidence evidence of the older source; no equivalence, shipping or Tacview claim until measured. D3 and Task 51 stay open, with Tasks 49 and 50 and the remaining services; D4/D5 unstarted.

returned, header/data open attempts and results, header count and matches, catalogue counts and digest, loader calls, the constructor's descriptor reads). The census of references to the descriptor table is in the documentation (source; compiled file vs executable block distinguished; commented and debug-excluded references are not active readers; no part of the playback code is called dormant; runtime liveness not measured); notably `speech.c` keeps only samples with `size > 0`, so a future host metadata table with real sizes would change the speech
stream and must be introduced deliberately.

# D3 host-owned sound lifetime — the two groups of the source review of 402ba4410 corrected (31 October 2026; source only, UNBUILT natively, UNRUN, UNREVIEWED)

Candidate `402ba441003e362486d3591c2d078f4a9b1d3bbf`; consolidated review `independent-environment-host-sound-lifetime-source-review-402ba4410-20261031.json` (SHA-256 `0b5f4680...f8cb`): ENV-HOST-SOUND-1 (P1) and ENV-HOST-SOUND-2 (P2). One focused uncommitted batch; **changed production C: a NEW immutable native is needed, never a 116 or 402 binary relabelled.** The 402 build/raw receipts and the 18 unused fresh roots are untouched; nothing ran natively.

**1 (P1) floating-point scope.** `env_ref_sound_init` / `env_ref_sound_update` no longer copy floats before `fp_save` or classify/assign them after `fp_leave`: outputs are initialised and published as bits (`memcpy`), floats are loaded after `fp_enter_canonical`, finiteness and sign are classified inside the scope into an integer flag, results are settled, the caller's state is restored and read back, then the staged bits are copied out. Expressions, order and stores unchanged; no global exception masking; no tolerance changed. The existing extended floating-point-state test (every pairing of rounding, precision, sticky flags, denormal modes and arranged status words, answers and complete caller state compared) now includes the refusals decided inside the scope: signalling NaN as lifetime, as delta and as an invalid effect's valid lifetime, a quiet NaN and an infinity.

**2 (P2) witness init modes.** The wrapper forwards every request unchanged while the delegate boots (the campaign's boot asks `sound_lifetime_init` for its looping ambient sounds) and counts the mode's operation apart as `boot_requests`; the alteration, refusal or malformed answer is armed only for the fixture phase (the phase turns at the return of the delegate's `dc.boot`, which is wrapped for the run and restored). `changed_init` therefore meets the case 6 constructor (0.25 in the real constructor state) and `withheld_init` stops at the case 6 `engine_failure` row; the scripted guards model the boot init requests (including the campaign's refusal of a non-zero looping lifetime). `changed` now reconciles the delegate's REAL entity words with the answers it sent: the constructor's lifetime word equals the word after every call (so the host's aging, not only its kill decision, is what the campaign applied) and nobody killed; `healthy` also requires an aged word after the first call; a native that asks the host but ages itself is `ownership-not-shown` (guard added). The delegate's grammar, rows and behavior are unchanged; the authority record gains `boot_requests` and `life_words`.

# D3 host-owned sound lifetime — first candidate extraction, source prepared (31 October 2026; UNBUILT natively, UNRUN, UNREVIEWED)

Clean HEAD `a53e71b365911d49a4df4b51982ef6952296b5e3`; the finite original-domain characterization is closed (native 116ffd5fb, drivers 2a/d4; combined actual review `89c26171...3d2`). **This batch moves the characterized ORIGINAL sound-lifetime decisions into the host** (EECH_WORLD reference), through two new operations of the existing public environment provider; one focused uncommitted batch. Not whole Task 51/D3.

**Moved (hosted EECH_DC; the classic `#else` keeps the original code):** `sound_lifetime_init` = the constructor's sum of the samples' durations, the 40 s / 300 s music cap and the looping case (`soundeff.c`); `sound_lifetime_update` = one call of `update_server` / `update_client`: the aging of a valid timed effect, the server's expiry and kill decision, the client's clamp at zero, and the countdown, zero crossing and next-update unlink of an invalid effect (`se_updt.c`). The reference kernels (`env_ref.c`, `env.rs`) are the original C expressions (same types and order, the engine's `max`/`min`) in the canonical arithmetic environment on staged copies, committed after the caller's FP state is restored and read back. The host keeps NO state.

**Exact data and why by value.** The request carries the sample descriptors' ints (rate, size) for a timed effect; the update request carries the delta (read where the original read it, so the previous/current delta phase is the original's), validity, looping flag, stored lifetime and valid lifetime, and whether a handle is held; a server's expired valid effect with a handle makes the host ask `need_playing` ONCE (nothing changed) and the campaign answers from its sound system. The stored lifetimes stay in the effect's record because pause/resume, the network pack/unpack and the observer read and write them: a host-held copy would diverge. The campaign writes both lifetimes from the CHECKED answer and then does what the host decided in the original order and at the original probe points (`ENV_FXE_*` hooks unchanged): kill, or unlink from the update list and release the handle. Answer checks before any write: finite numbers; only a valid timed effect's lifetime and an invalid effect's valid lifetime may change; an expiry belongs to a valid effect, a kill to the server's expired effect, an unlink to an invalid one; a looping effect's constructor lifetime is +0; a sequence of 0 or more than 16 samples is refused, not truncated. A missing provider, a refusal or a malformed answer stops the engine naming `[env-provider:sound_lifetime_*...]`; no campaign arithmetic remains in the hosted build.

## The P2 and the correction (validator and collaborator only; no C, engine, module, host-kernel or physical-input change)

`check_witness` accepted decoder call histories that cannot occur, and so did the stand-in's healthy input: for example `g_calls=2 g_true=2 g_last=1 g_depth=0` (a hit at depth 0 asks once), later depths with the same calls,
and the exhausted `g_calls=3 g_true=2 g_last=0 g_depth=1` (an exhausted walk asks 6 times yes and once no). The report buckets are recomputed from the same fields, so coherent buckets did not prove a possible call sequence.
The 18-guard positive accepted that input: a known checker weakness, not a native physical failure.

New rule in `lua/collision-characterization.lua` (after all the older bounds and hit implications, which are unchanged), for the FIXED 6-triangle model, with F = `g_calls - g_true`:
`g_true = 6 * F + (g_last == 1 ? g_depth + 1 : 0)`; and when `g_true > 0` and `g_last == 0` the last yes is at depth 5. A query that never asked keeps the neutral zero depth. It checks call-history conservation only, not
an intersection or any answer. Root's independent audit of the actual native histories (`R:/d3-evidence/geometry-47a-native-history-conservation-audit.json`: Georgia 4802, each Lebanon 5126, ZERO violations, original trace
hashes unchanged) agrees; no native campaign or witness is re-run for this.

Diagnostics (new): `tq N: g_true T is impossible: F completed walks of 6 triangles and a final walk that hit at depth D / did not hit make E` and `tq N: an exhausted walk's last yes is at depth 5, g_depth is D`. The existing
diagnostics (`g_true … more than g_calls`, never-answered with a last answer or depth, last yes without a hit, depth outside the model) keep their text and order ahead of them.

## Collaborator (stand-in) and guards

* Healthy histories are now POSSIBLE ones (`walk_history`): geometry hits at depth 0 to 5 after none, one or two complete walks of other trees; a hit through the quad path after one or two complete walks (g_last 0,
  depth 5); true misses after one to three complete walks; and no-call misses. The report buckets are still derived from the same fields.
* Six new single-defect modes, each with COHERENT report buckets so that only the new rule can reject them (tests in `tests/host_callbacks.rs`; the guard array grows from 20 to 26):

| mode | history | expected reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `witness_history_true_count` | calls 2, true 2, last 1, depth 0 | `tq 0: g_true 2 is impossible: 0 completed walks of 6 triangles and a final walk that hit at depth 0 make 1` |
| `witness_history_final_depth` | calls 2, true 2, last 1, depth 3 | `tq 0: g_true 2 is impossible: 0 completed walks of 6 triangles and a final walk that hit at depth 3 make 4` |
| `witness_history_incomplete_walk` | calls 3, true 2, last 0, depth 1 | `g_true 2 is impossible: 1 completed walks of 6 triangles and a final walk that did not hit make 6` |
| `witness_history_exhausted_depth` | calls 7, true 6, last 0, depth 4 | `an exhausted walk's last yes is at depth 5, g_depth is 4` |
| `witness_history_calls_without_true` | calls 3, true 0, last 0, depth 0 | `g_true 0 is impossible: 3 completed walks of 6 triangles and a final walk that did not hit make 18` |
| `witness_history_zero_call_depth` | calls 0, true 0, last 0, depth 2 | `a query the geometry branch never answered has a last answer or a depth` (the older rule: refused by the OLD driver too) |

## The corrections (source only; no mesh, vertex, original math, call order, baseline, tolerance or host-kernel change)

* State representation (1): in `probe_run_body`, `trace_witness = witness_active` is set immediately AFTER `trace_reset_records()` (which does not touch it) in the same `if (trace_armed)` block that rebuilds the facts, and the
  assignment inside `trace_build_facts` is removed. The flag therefore always describes the records held: a controlled probe's pages carry the geometry fields; a default probe on the same arming writes the old
  bytes again; arming still clears it. A probe that does not touch the transcript leaves records and flag together.
* One-shot at every entered refusal (2 and 3), at each layer, with no ambient/session framework:

  * `Engine::collision_probe` (Rust): the body moved to `collision_probe_entered`; ANY `Err` (the range refusal before C, the engine's refusals, the report refusals) clears the arming with `collision_geometry_arm(false)`
    (idempotent; its own failure is ignored because an engine that is not running cannot be armed).
  * Lua method `collision_probe` (eech-dc): it now takes the raw argument list (`mlua::MultiValue`) and converts it INSIDE the method with `FromLuaMulti` into the same `(u32, i32, i32)`, the same scalar conversions and
    coercions the typed signature used; any error (conversion, engine) clears the arming and the original error is returned unchanged. The error TEXT of a conversion refusal can differ in its argument-position prefix from the
    typed signature's, since mlua adds that prefix only for typed arguments; the refusal itself and the engine's reasons are unchanged. No `RefCell` or other borrow is held across the conversion, which can run Lua metamethods.
  A completed probe still consumes the arming in C; a successful probe never clears anything extra.
* No new test double: the three real scripts above are the boundary tests (a mock would only prove its own setup). The 18 portable driver guards and the 3 argument refusals are unchanged.

# Original forest-tree GEOMETRY witness — source PREPARED, UNBUILT, UNRUN, unreviewed (EEDCS-49, D3 characterization before the model-loading extraction)

This completes the partial checkpoint 5154bc7e7 (the feature-only observation hook in `en_cllsn.c`) into a bounded, controlled witness of the ORIGINAL forest-tree geometry branch and the ORIGINAL
model-triangle decoder. Nothing here was built, formatted, tested or run. The measured host tree preparation at `8c452f197449d3a08b8f7bfbad5c34ae652c22c1` (below) is unchanged and not re-reviewed;
no host kernel, loader or Lua API file was touched. Production dispatch is unchanged; the shipping expansion of the new macro is exactly the original call. Task47 shipping115 is untouched.
Task49 and D3 remain In Progress; the model loader, the host geometry branch's agreement with the original, entity collision, G1 integration, production authority and the DCS mapping remain open.

## Why

The measured retail maps give the forest tree object NO collision triangles (`tf-forest geometry=0`), so the original's type-1 geometry branch of `get_line_of_sight_collision_tree` has never run against
them: the 554/600/600 exact replays prove the quad path only. The host kernel carries the geometry branch as the original's text but unexercised, and the model-loading responsibility cannot be moved
before the ORIGINAL's decoder and branch have been measured on a known input.

## What the witness is (all answers are the original code's)

* Input (environment, constants, labelled controlled): a fixture-owned model of 12 points, 3 faces (a quad, a triangle and a pentagon, so fan order and depth order), 2 surfaces whose per-surface point tables are
  not the identity (surface 0 permutes its 7 entries, surface 1 restarts local indexes at 0 with 5), 16-bit points scaled by a bounding box of x/z plus or minus 0.25 and y 0 to 1, and the zero SENTINEL surface the original
  reads after the last face of the last surface. It makes 6 triangles (4-gon: 2, triangle: 1, 5-gon: 3). Decoded coordinates, fan order, scaling and the walk are produced ONLY by the original
  `get_object_3d_collision_object_geometry_triangle`; the fixture never decodes, intersects or predicts.
* Seam: the original reads the model through `objects_3d_data[objects_3d_scene_database[FOREST_TREE_OBJECT].collision_object_index]`. Index 0 (the retail null object, which the accepted C1 patch maps to -1) is NOT used.
  The witness copies the real object table (`total_number_of_raw_3d_objects + 1` entries, content identical, checked), appends its own object after the last real index, points `objects_3d_data` at the copy and
  sets only the forest scene's `collision_object_index` to the appended index, for exactly one probe. Entity queries see an identical table; no real object, tree, file, list or position is changed; the real type-1
  trees of the loaded map are the trees.
* Restoration (every path: normal, the body's own refusals, report too big): the scene index and the `objects_3d_data` pointer are put back FIRST, the copy is freed AFTER. The report then states `data_restored`
  (pointer), `scene_restored` (index), `copy_identical`, the hash of the WHOLE real object table before/after, the hash of the forest scene entry before/after and the scene index before/after; the driver
  requires every one, and a failed restoration is a failed run with the raw report kept (`report_invalid`).
* Observation: `en_cllsn.c`'s two reads of the decoder go through `TREE_QUERY_GEOMETRY_TRIANGLE`; under `EECH_COLLISION_FIXTURE` it calls the fixture wrapper, which calls the original decoder once, with the same
  arguments in the same order, and records by value (calls, yes answers, last answer, depth of the last yes). No extra decoder, terrain or intersection query exists. From it: per stage (0 primary cold, 1 primary warm,
  2 nearer-check cold, 3 nearer-check warm) the queries made, those that ENTERED the branch, those that HIT through it (the first successful triangle returns at once), those that hit through the quad path although geometry
  was present, and those that walked a tree's triangles to the end; and for stage 0 which triangle depth hit.
* One-shot arming: `engine:collision_geometry_arm(true)` (new, feature-only, mirroring `collision_trace_arm`) applies to the NEXT `collision_probe` and is consumed by it whatever its outcome, so no disarm path exists.
  The driver gets `geometry_witness=yes` (requires `probe=yes` and `trace_out`; anything else is refused before booting).

## Default (witness off) is unchanged

The unarmed probe is the original probe body byte for byte (it was only renamed and wrapped): same report rows, same transcript rows and bytes. The new row, fact row and per-query fields exist only when armed. In
the driver, without `geometry_witness=yes` a `col-geometry-witness` row, a `tf-witness` row or a `g_*` field is an UNKNOWN row/key and is refused, so the reviewed f3 default reports (205 ordinary values, 206 trace-report
rows) must still compare byte for byte; Root's native default run is the proof, not this statement.

## New report/transcript shape (checks, not physical answers)

* Report row `col-geometry-witness`: `label=controlled_forest_geometry source=fixture_owned_mesh installed restored data_restored scene_restored copy_identical objects_count scene_index_before scene_index_after
  objects_before objects_after entry_before entry_after mesh_points=12 mesh_faces=3 mesh_surfaces=2 mesh_triangles=6 mesh_fold` then `q0 b0 g0 o0 e0 ... q3 b3 g3 o3 e3` and `d0..d7 dbeyond`.
* Transcript: `trace-start` carries `geometry_witness=controlled_forest_geometry`; a `tf-witness` facts row; `tf-forest geometry=1 triangles=6` with 6 `tf-triangle` rows (the ORIGINAL's decoded output); every `tq` row gains
  `g_calls g_true g_last g_depth`. Everything else (tf-map, tf-sample, caller bits, ordered terrain lookups, final hit/point/normal bits) is the existing format, so `tests/tree_conformance.rs` and
  `lua/tree-collision-replay.lua` replay the SAME transcript (the Lua replay now accepts recorded triangles; it still refuses a capped, miscounted or out-of-order list).
* Driver checks: exactly the labels/mesh constants above; `restored` and the four identity elements; `tf-forest geometry=1`, `triangles=6`; per query `g_true <= g_calls`, a never-answered branch has no last answer or depth,
  a last yes is a hit, `g_depth < 6`; and the report's per-stage `q/b/g/o/e` and depth counts must EQUAL the same counts recomputed from the transcript's per-query facts.
* Named coverage gaps (never a pass, `require_coverage=yes` fails on them): `geometry_branch_never_entered`, `no_geometry_hit`, `no_geometry_hit_after_the_first_triangle`, `geometry_walk_never_exhausted`,
  `no_geometry_query_miss`, `no_geometry_miss_with_a_partial_write`, `geometry_branch_not_seen_with_flags_<ignore_edge>_<skip_top>` for each of the four flag combinations. Event `geometry_witness_coverage` carries the counts.

## Measured state of the 684fb6981 source (retained; this does NOT cover the new code)

684fb6981 already measured: Windows 17/17 units, 1/1 real-host Lua transport, ALL 554/600/600 original queries with 1102/1120/1120 lookups exact through the library (default and Up/Down/Zero callers with non-zero
exception status restored) AND Lua, all 3 pre/post manifests 0 and all 8 payloads unchanged; Root's unchanged protocol script passing all 6 cases. Linux 17/17 units, Lua transport and fmt passed and Clippy exit 101 on three
style lints; those three fixes (as_chunks, expect_err, a local `Case` alias) are PREPARED in the working tree, UNCOMMITTED, UNBUILT, UNRUN and are preserved here.

## The seam (found by the same reviewer's closure of the five pending-query/protocol fixes only)

`begin` abandoned the OLD pending query before it read its Lua fields, but reading a field can run Lua (`__index`). A getter can re-enter `host.tree_collision` with a VALID begin and then raise an error or return a
malformed `old_position`: the OUTER begin is refused, but the NESTED query it created survives and a later `terrain` continues it. Root's actual RED on the frozen 684 host (SHA256
706f4b39b005381a447421a03531297f425c0c2162938decded246db3615fd43; private `R:/d3-evidence/tree-host-reentrant-red-684fb6981-20261029/controller.json`; script
`R:/d3-evidence/tree-host-reentrant-begin-control-20261029.lua` SHA256 2bb59f7553686b0edc9a3d253d6c7b05866effc04e8b1055aff46a193b058244, to be replayed UNCHANGED against the next host): each real getter ran
exactly once; `getter_error` and `getter_malformed` each gave outer accepted=false but continued=true / `need_terrain` (ghost continuation); `healthy_reentry` gave outer accepted=true, continued=true. All 3 diagnostic
native processes exited 0. These observe the bug; they are not pass claims.

## The cleanup (source only; no formula, FPU, loader, physical or protocol change)

`src/main.rs`, `host.tree_collision{mode='begin'}`: the whole argument parse AND the call into the kernel now run inside one small `Result` scope; EVERY `Err` leaving that scope abandons whatever is pending AT THAT
MOMENT (including a nested query the getter started) before the error is returned. The earlier pre-parse abandon stays (it still closes the old query on an ordinary malformed request). No `RefCell` borrow is held
while Lua runs: each borrow is taken for one call and dropped, so a re-entering getter never meets a held borrow. There is no recursion ban and no transaction framework, so the healthy control is unchanged: a getter
that starts a nested query and then returns a valid vector still yields an accepted outer begin that replaces the nested query and continues. `terrain` already abandoned after a parse error and still does.

Real-host controls added to `tests/tree_collision_host.rs` (all old protocol, tiny / negative-zero and geometry checks kept): a metatable getter that starts a valid nested begin and then (a) errors, (b) returns a 2-element
`old_position`: the outer begin is refused, the getter ran exactly once and the next `terrain` is refused with "no query open"; (c) returns a valid vector: the outer begin is accepted and the request continues to the new
end point.

  (ghost continuations). A healthy pending request continues. These are measured defects, not pass claims.

## The single independent review's batch, and what the prepared source does (source only; arithmetic untouched — the reviewer found NO discrepancy between the C and the original arithmetic)

1. P2 map invariant. `TreeMap`'s public fields let a forged value bypass `new()` (for example min_x = max_x = f32::MAX with 2 sectors could reach an undefined C float-to-int conversion; the reviewer did not execute that malformed native query). The invariant is
   now REVALIDATED: `TreeMap::validate()` (the checks of `new`, which now calls it) is called first by EVERY public scene constructor: `without_trees`, `from_bytes`, and `load` including its absent-file path.
   Valid metadata and all math unchanged. Unit test `a_tree_map_built_by_hand_is_revalidated_by_every_scene_constructor` feeds nine forged literals to all four paths (none is executed in C) and checks the valid map
   and an empty triangle list; an empty `Triangles(vec![])` is itself refused (it is not a statement about the geometry).
2. P2 complete caller floating-point state. On the Windows toolchain `fesetenv` did not give back MXCSR (the SSE rounding stayed round-toward-zero and the inexact flag stayed raised). The C entry now saves the x87
   environment (`fegetenv`) AND the whole MXCSR (`stmxcsr`: control and status bits), sets round-toward-zero in both units and reads both back, runs the original arithmetic, and on EVERY exit restores with
   `fesetenv` then `ldmxcsr` and reads MXCSR back; a restore (or set) that does not read back as expected is `TREE_ENVIRONMENT`: the answer is withheld and the query closed. The exception masks are saved/restored
   exactly and never weakened; unmasked callers are still refused up front. `ScopedRounding` uses the same save/restore. `FpState` now also carries the raw x87 control word and raw MXCSR. The library and the
   real-query tests now enter from callers in each rounding mode with a NON-CLEAR exception status (inexact and divide-by-zero raised before the call; asserted non-zero) and compare masks, rounding, raw control
   words, raw MXCSR and raised flags before and after. An actual unmasked-exception entry and an actual `fesetround`/`fesetenv`/`ldmxcsr` failure are NOT exercised and not claimed.
3. P2 thread affinity. `ScopedRounding` carries a `PhantomData<*const ()>`, so it is neither `Send` nor `Sync`. A compile-time contract in the unit tests (the `AmbiguousIfSend`/`AmbiguousIfSync` technique of the
   static_assertions crate, no new dependency) fails the test build if either bound is ever implemented.
4. P2 dense geometry. `host.tree_collision{mode='load'}` requires `forest_geometry` to be `"absent"` or a DENSE ordered list (`dense_length`: every key an integer 1..n, no hole or extra key) of triangles that are
   each a dense list of exactly nine numbers; a sparse, holey, empty or malformed list is refused BEFORE any geometry is discarded or absence is assumed, and a refused load leaves the loaded scene untouched. Host
   script controls: `{[2]=tri}`, `{[1]=tri,[3]=tri}`, `{}`, an eight-number triangle, a holey triangle and a non-table item are refused; `{tri, tri}` and `"absent"` are accepted. No physical oracle was added and
   native geometry is not claimed validated.
5. P2 pending-query cleanup. The Lua `begin` abandons any pending query BEFORE parsing its arguments (a begin replaces the pending query anyway), and a `terrain` whose elevation cannot be read abandons it; in Rust a
   non-finite `terrain` answer closes the pending query. Contract: a refused begin or terrain answer ends the pending query, so a later valid `terrain` is refused with "no query open"; a refused `load` changes
   neither the scene nor a pending query. The real-host script covers pending -> malformed begin, pending -> non-boolean flag, pending -> non-finite elevation, pending -> non-numeric elevation, and the healthy
   pending control that continues. Root's unchanged protocol script above is the second check.
6. P3 negative zero. The synthetic script constructs it as `-1 / math.huge` and asserts `1 / negative_zero == -math.huge`; the expected `80000000` and the numeric reader are unchanged.
7. P3 loader wording. The module documentation no longer says "before anything is allocated": it says the two files are read whole, each size is first checked against `MAX_SECTOR_FILE_BYTES` and
   `MAX_DATA_FILE_BYTES` (a bound on what `fs::read` allocates; retail Georgia is 226 KB and 6.8 MB), the forest triangles are flattened as given, and every length, multiplication and span is checked in `u64`
   with sector-table byte sizes checked before allocating that table and each sector's record span checked before tree-record decoding or indexing. No format change.

# Host tree kernel — first native checks FAILED (real RED); rounding-environment correction PREPARED, UNBUILT, UNRUN (EEDCS-49, D3 preparation)

## What the first native checks of source 0db20ab3a46582110bd7c4706c26edaaa9335478 actually showed (retained; terminal; NOT passed)

* Windows build 0, all 8 exported manifest entries verified; frozen binary `…/eech-campaign/target/tree-host/0db20ab3a`; controller `tree-host-first-windows-0db20ab3a-20261029-completion.json`.
* Linux: 14/14 tree library unit tests pass; the real-host Lua transport test FAILED at its assertion `both outside: no lookups at all` (Linux invocation exit 101; Clippy not reached). Windows: 14/14 tree
  library units pass; the same Lua transport test FAILED. Raw log `tree-host-first-linux-0db20ab3a-20261029.log`.
* Windows replay of ALL 554 Georgia / 600 Lebanon / 600 repeat captured queries with their 1102 / 1120 / 1120 recorded terrain replies, through BOTH the library path (exit 101) and the host Lua path
  (exit 1) on each scenario: the loader, census and native samples agreed, but OUTPUT BITS DIFFERED. The retained diagnostic list is bounded (its 41 entries are not the number of failing queries).
  First actual tq 0 Georgia point `45e0dec9,41ed10b2,48584704` against the original `45e0dec9,41ed10b2,48584703`; other retained examples differ by one bit in x, y or z. Raw per-case logs and
  controller JSON under `R:/d3-evidence/tree-host-first-0db20ab3a-native-20261029`; all 3 pre/post manifests 0, all 8 payloads and every original transcript hash unchanged. The raw expected data is
  unchanged and is the oracle.

## Diagnosis (two separate defects; neither is a change to the original's physics)

1. MISSING ENVIRONMENT BOUNDARY (the numerical failure). The original runs under round-toward-zero: `eech_engine.c` ENTER saves the caller's `fenv` and sets `FE_TOWARDZERO`, LEAVE and the fatal path restore
   it, the collision fixture refuses captures unless `fegetround() == FE_TOWARDZERO`, and the original `get_terrain_3d_sector` sets it again. The first source read and required only the exception masks
   (63/63) and explicitly left rounding alone, so it executed under the caller's ordinary round-to-nearest, which is not equivalent. Masks of 63/63 do not establish rounding.
2. WRONG SYNTHETIC EXPECTATION in `tests/tree_collision_host.rs` (a test defect, not a kernel defect). The case `{-1,10,1024} -> {5000,10,1024}` was expected to miss because "both outside: no lookups". The
   segment runs along z = 1024 at y = 10 and actually CROSSES the tree at the middle of sector (0,0). An end point outside the map only avoids the terrain lookup for that end (its radial altitude is
   taken as 0 / the old one's); it never makes the collision FALSE, and a `done` answer with no `need_terrain` first simply means no lookup was needed. The test now asserts the real contract: that
   segment gives `done` immediately with a HIT at the hand-derived point (1024, 10, 1024), normal +x; and a both-outside segment that crosses no tree (z = 3000) gives `done`, a miss, and the caller's own
   point and normal. The original behaviour was not changed to suit the old expectation. The assertions after that point in the script had not been reached by the failed run; they were re-read against the
   source and the kernel text (ordering, refusals, exact tiny / negative-zero reads) and no further defect was found by reading, which is not a run.

## The correction (source only; math, loader, query and scan order, partial writes, tie rules, triangles and recorded data untouched)

`csrc/tree_step.c`: the former `eech_tree_begin` / `eech_tree_terrain` bodies are now private `noinline` functions, and each public entry wraps them (the pattern of the host-private terrain_ref.c of G1, not imported):
1. read the x87 and SSE exception masks and REQUIRE 63 and 63 BEFORE any arithmetic; on failure return `TREE_MASKS`, compute nothing, change nothing, and the query is closed. The kernel never masks exceptions.
2. `fegetenv` the caller's environment; `fesetround(FE_TOWARDZERO)`; either failing is `TREE_ENVIRONMENT` (the caller's environment is put back if it was touched).
3. run the original's arithmetic (begin: the in-map tests, radial altitudes, scan; terrain: the radial altitude and scan).
4. `fesetenv` the caller's environment on EVERY exit: lookup request, final answer, scene fault, masks refusal path (nothing set), environment failure. If the restore itself fails the answer is withheld,
   the query is closed and the call returns `TREE_ENVIRONMENT`. An out-of-sequence `terrain` returns before touching the environment.
No guard state exists between calls, so none is held across the Lua/campaign callbacks that supply elevations. The bodies are not inlined into the entries so no arithmetic is scheduled outside the guard. The file is
deliberately NOT built with `-frounding-math`: the original's compile-time constant folds (e.g. `19/127.0f`, `PI2 - 0.01`) happened at the default rounding; the host must fold the same constants the same way.
Whether this reproduces the original is established only by Root's replay of the captured queries, not by reasoning.
`src/trees.rs`: the Rust-side mask check is removed (the C entry is authoritative); codes -3 / -4 map to clear errors; new public environment helpers `rounding()`, `Rounding`, `exception_flags()`,
`clear_exception_flags()` and the RAII `ScopedRounding` (saves and restores the whole caller environment) exist only to enter the kernel from a caller in another mode in tests and reports.

## New boundary checks (all source only)

* Library unit test `the_answer_does_not_depend_on_the_callers_rounding_and_the_callers_environment_is_restored`: five hand-derived-class cases (plane hit with division and normalisation, top-quad hit, a miss,
  a both-outside segment that still hits with no lookup, a geometry-branch triangle hit) entered from a caller in Nearest, Up, Down and Zero; answers and lookup requests compared as bits across all four,
  the caller's rounding checked after EVERY call into the kernel (including after a lookup request), and masks, rounding and raised exception flags compared before and after.

## Changed files (all under `eech-campaign/crates/eech-world/`)

* `csrc/tree_step.c` — NEW. The host-private C kernel: EECH's own `get_line_of_sight_collision_tree` (en_cllsn.c) with `get_3d_line_quad_intersection` and
  `get_3d_line_triangle_intersection` (maths/vector.c), expression for expression, as a resumable NeedTerrain/Done state machine. Built with the existing `eech_steps` flags and `eech_arith.h`.
